blocks.text: Every monster in Unwritten is a **blank page** — one of the pages that should have carried the rest of the world's record and never did, given hostile form. That's why they appear **flat and papery**: their two-dimensional look isn't a style choice — it's what they *are*. To defeat one is to **fill it in**: one more line of the record that now exists because you wrote it.

items: **By biome** — each biome (Grassland, Snow, Desert, Volcanic, Corrupted) has its own family of monsters. See *World & Maps*.

**By level** — every monster has a level, exactly like you do. That single number is what makes it dangerous; there is no separate difficulty rating. A zone draws from a range of levels, so where a place sits in the world tells you what it will throw at you.
**By size** — monsters are **Small, Medium, or Large**, which is meant to interact with your weapon type (see *Combat Mechanics*).

blocks.text: A monster is not built from a different set of numbers than you are. It has the **same six stats**, grown by the **same formulas**, and — this is the part that matters — it gets the **same number of stat points its level allows**. A level 20 monster is carrying exactly what a level 20 player could have bought. Nothing is inflated behind the scenes and nothing is quietly weakened.

items: **It wears real equipment** — the same gear you can wear, in the same slots. A monster's strength is its level, its stats, and its kit.
**It can wear a Ring** — and if it does, that Ring's investment scales it on the same soft-cap curve yours uses. A ringed monster is a genuinely different fight.
**Its stats are visible in its numbers** — a monster that hits hard has the attack to prove it. There is no hidden multiplier making things tougher.

blocks.text: Because a monster is built like a character, anything a skill can do to you it can do to a monster — and the reverse. A monster can be slowed, shielded, guarded, drained, or pulled off its feet just as you can.
Drops — they drop what they wear

A monster's equipment **is** its loot table. Hover over it, or fight it, and its panel at the top of the screen lists every piece it wears and the chance that piece falls — the rarer the piece, the smaller the chance. What falls lands on the ground where it died: for 10 seconds only the player who earned the kill can pick it up, then anyone can, and it vanishes after a minute if nobody does. Coin goes straight into your purse.

items: **Worn gear** — each piece it carries rolls on its own, so a well-equipped monster is worth hunting.
**Materials** — fangs, hides, and the like. No stats of their own; they feed **Crafting & Recycling**.
**Rings** — vanishingly rare, roughly **1 in 100,000**. A Ring is the single most valuable thing anything can carry, so treat one dropping as the story of your week.
**Bosses** are larger, self-assembled masses of blank page — absence gathered into something powerful and deliberate.
**The silencer** is the thing that stopped the scribe mid-sentence — the reason any page was left blank, and the deepest blankness in the world.
